archetype.name: Game Manager (quick-game backup)
archetype.definition: A short-area distributor who keeps the ball out of harm's way and moves the offense on schedule, but holds it too long under pressure and rarely threatens defenses vertically, the kind of spot starter Baltimore keeps turning to when Lamar Jackson is down.

report.headline: Steady, safe spot starter whose sacks erase his gains, now stuck on IR
report.take:
Huntley is what he has been for six seasons: a backup who completes a lot of passes and very rarely throws them to the other team. His 69.1% completion rate ranks 7th of 54 qualifiers, his 0.9% interception rate ranks 9th, and his 2.94 CPOE sits 4.2 points over the league average. As a starter in Weeks 5-7 he was a perfectly functional quarterback: 221.3 passing yards a game, +0.106 EPA per dropback and 17.5 PPR points, with Baltimore going 1-2. Nobody should mistake that for a hidden starter, but it was comfortably above the league-average dropback (-0.021).

The value did not come from where the completion rate suggests. Throws under 10 air yards, which are most of his attempts, completed 77.8% of the time but added only +0.043 EPA a play. The real production came from the intermediate area: 22 attempts at 10-19 yards produced +0.495 EPA a play and 10.9 total EPA despite a 54.5% completion rate. Deep he was 1-of-7. Throws to the left (+0.374) carried him, while the middle of the field (-17.1 CPOE) was a dead zone. Rashod Bateman (+0.611 per target) and Josh Cuevas (+0.557) produced with him. Mark Andrews (-0.62 per target, -9.3 total) and Justice Hill (-0.32) were where drives went to die.

The number that undoes him is the sack. His 9.1% sack rate ranks 40th of 54 and his 39.3% pressure-to-sack rate 36th, and that is not new. He ranked 55th of 62 in pressure-to-sack in 2021 and 49th in both 2022 and 2025. He holds the ball (2.84-second time to throw) without converting the extra time into scrambles of value: 9 scrambles, zero first downs. That is why his passing EPA (4.2 total) turns into a negative 1.1 across all 131 dropbacks. Last year's 12.9 CPOE and 10.4% bad-throw rate were the outlier, not the baseline. This year's 17.3% bad-throw rate, ranked 36th of 42, looks much more like the 2021 version of him.

Where it goes from here depends almost entirely on availability. He is listed on injured reserve, did not practice in Week 9 and sits fifth on the depth chart as of Nov. 17. Jackson's thumb surgery has him projected back around late December. The dossier's start list also credits Huntley with Week 10, with no game line attached, so his exact timeline is murky. When healthy he is the most proven fill-in on this roster. On the evidence, though, he is a floor-raiser, not someone who changes Baltimore's ceiling.

strengths.title: Ball security on short throws
strengths.body: A 0.9% interception rate (9th of 54) comes from a quick-game approach. His intended air yards sit at 6.69, 2.25 short of the sticks, and a quarter of his attempts were thrown behind the line. That keeps the offense out of disaster plays. It is a durable trait: he has thrown 0 picks in two of his last three seasons.

strengths.title: Intermediate throws carry the offense
strengths.body: His 22 throws at 10-19 air yards produced more EPA than the rest of his passing combined, at +0.495 per play. He is accurate enough to hit windows to the left side and the boundary, which is where Bateman and Cuevas did their damage. On a small sample it will likely cool, but it shows he can do more than check the ball down.

strengths.title: Competent full-game starter
strengths.body: Across his three Weeks 5-7 starts he ran a positive-EPA passing game at +0.106 per dropback, and he posted 3-plus passing EPA in each of those games, including against a Cleveland defense now ranked 9th. That is a steady, unspectacular floor that has held up across his Ravens stints.

concerns.title: Pressure turns into sacks
concerns.body: He takes a sack on 39.3% of pressured dropbacks (36th of 42), and 19.7% of his dropbacks end with a hit or a sack. That is a career-long trait, not a slump, and his scrambling no longer pays it back: 9 scrambles have produced zero first downs. It is the main reason his total dropback EPA lands below zero despite positive passing EPA.

concerns.title: Accuracy drifting back to career norm
concerns.body: His bad-throw rate jumped 6.9 points from last year to 17.3%. Game by game it climbed from 9.7% to 19.4% to 23.5% across his three starts. Next Gen's model has his completion rate 3.24 points below expected once throw difficulty is accounted for, so the box-score completion rate flatters him. Last season's precision looks like the blip.

concerns.title: No vertical or middle game
concerns.body: He completed 1 of 7 deep throws, and middle-of-field throws came in at -17.1 CPOE. Andrews, a seam target by trade, produced -9.3 EPA on his 15 targets. Defenses can sit on the boundaries and the short area, which caps how far Baltimore's offense can climb with him.

trend.note: His passing EPA held between 3.4 and 4.2 in each of his three starts, but CPOE slid from +6.4 to the negatives and the bad-throw rate climbed every week. Then a Week 8 relief appearance at Buffalo went to pieces: pressured on 80% of his dropbacks, -7.4 EPA on four throws, a lost fumble. His last three games cost him 4.5 points of CPOE against his season mark, and he has been on IR since.

nextGame.headline: Soft pass rush in Carolina, but IR likely keeps him off the field
nextGame.body:
On paper Carolina is close to an ideal matchup for his flaw. The Panthers rank 32nd in both defensive hit rate and sack rate, so the pressure that turns into his sacks should be scarce. Their pass defense ranks 23rd in EPA. The catch is that they allow explosive passes at the 2nd-lowest rate in the league and are 4th-stingiest against opposing WR1s. That pushes the game toward his short-to-intermediate habits rather than letting Zay Flowers run free. Tight ends and lead backs have done well against them (both 27th in points over their usual output), though Andrews has not converted with Huntley throwing.

Availability decides everything. Huntley is listed on injured reserve and fifth on the depth chart, so he should not be expected to play, and Jackson's thumb timeline points to late December. On Baltimore's side, guard Olaivavega Ioane (91% of snaps) is questionable with a shoulder, which matters to any Ravens quarterback. Carolina will be without linebacker Bobby Okereke (89% of snaps) and corner Will Lee III (73%), with corner Mike Jackson on IR. That thins a secondary that has been the strength of its defense.

keyMatchups.title: Weakest pass rush he could face
keyMatchups.body: Carolina's 4.3% sack rate is the league's lowest, and its hit rate also ranks last. For a quarterback whose sacks wipe out his passing value, this is the matchup that hides his biggest flaw. Whoever starts for Baltimore benefits.

keyMatchups.title: Depleted Panthers secondary and linebackers
keyMatchups.body: Losing Will Lee III and Mike Jackson at corner and Okereke at linebacker opens the intermediate and middle areas. The intermediate area is where Huntley does his best work, and the middle is where he has struggled most.

keyMatchups.title: Tight ends against a soft spot
keyMatchups.body: Carolina gives up +0.4 EPA a play to opposing TE1s, 26th in the league. Cuevas has been efficient with Huntley, at +0.557 per target, even as Andrews has not.

nextGame.watch: Whether Huntley is activated from IR at all. If not, the Carolina matchup belongs to whichever quarterback Baltimore turns to.

restOfSeason.body:
The rest of his season comes down to two calendars: his own return from IR and Jackson's, projected around late December. If he gets healthy before Jackson, he is the likely bridge starter, and the version to expect is the Weeks 5-7 one. That means short, high-percentage passing, few interceptions and a sack-heavy floor, landing around 180-225 passing yards and 0.8-1.4 touchdowns in a start. Rushing has faded from his earlier seasons, so 12-25 yards a game is the realistic band.

What should hold is the low interception rate and the completion volume, since both are rooted in how short he throws. What should regress is the intermediate efficiency, which rests on 22 attempts and will cool. The sack problem is the most stable thing in his profile and will keep dragging down his dropback efficiency. Once Jackson returns, Huntley goes back to the bench, and his fantasy value is limited to whatever spot starts land in between.
swingFactors: His activation from IR and depth-chart standing
Interior line health (Ioane) against the pressure that sacks him

confidence.note: Only 110 attempts, a murky injury and depth status, and no clear path to starts.
